english.title: Use a motor vehicle / trailer when the rear registration mark was not lit during darkness
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), during the hours of darkness a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), when not every letter and number of the registration mark displayed on the back of

(A)_[the]_
(B)_[the trailer drawn by the]_
(C)_[the rearmost trailer drawn by the]_

vehicle was illuminated so as to be easily legible as prescribed by Regulation 9 of the Road Vehicles (Display of Registration Marks) Regulations 2001
english.legislation: Contrary to section 59(1) of the Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also offence wordings: H643 and H779.
(ii) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(iii) Additional information may be included in the Statement of Facts specifying whether the lamp was blown, the wiring was loose or there was a poor battery, etc.
(iv) Fixed penalty scheme may be applied.
(v) Regulation 9(1) of the Road Vehicles (Display of Registration Marks) Regulations 2001 provides that this offence does not apply to works trucks, road rollers, agricultural machines and vehicle first registered before 1/11/1938.
english.standardstatementoffacts:
At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) the defendant used on **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..) during the hours of darkness **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..). The whole registration mark displayed on the back of

(A)_[the]_
(B)_[the trailer drawn by the]_
(C)_[the rearmost trailer drawn by the]_

vehicle was not illuminated so that it was easily legible.
